title: Runbook and Acceptance Criteria for Session-aware SLOs with Canary Dose-scaling and Tenant-weighted Burn
creator: Aisha Kapoor
description:
Purpose: Define a PRD-level runbook and acceptance criteria for introducing session-aware SLOs that account for multi-turn conversational state, together with a conservative canary 'dose-scaling' rollout strategy and tenant-weighted error-budget burn policies.

Background: Current SLO definitions are per-request and do not account for session persistence (KV cache warm-ness) or multi-model fallbacks. As we roll out the quantized and fallback model variants, we need precise acceptance criteria to avoid regressions during progressive releases. This ticket consolidates requirements, defines measurable metrics, and prescribes a controlled canary dosing plan that scales traffic proportionally while enforcing per-tenant fairness.

Scope:
- Define session-aware latency bands (p50/p95/p99) and availability targets for interactive chat routes and multi-turn sessions.
- Specify error-budget computation that weights multi-turn sessions higher (session length penalty) and includes fallback errors from model chains.
- Design the canary dose-scaling rollout (0% -> 1% -> 5% -> 20% -> 50% -> 100%) with automated gate checks and synthetic probe windows.
- Create monitoring dashboards, alerting thresholds, and an automated rollback policy tied to burn rates and probe failures.
- Provide acceptance criteria, runbook steps, and handoff artifacts for Eng/QA/SRE.

Out of scope: Billing model changes, dedicated capacity autoscaler tuning, and deep host-level kernel selection — those are tracked in separate ENG epics.

Deliverables: PRD/Runbook doc, acceptance criteria checklist, Grafana dashboard templates, synthetic test set & probe harness, CI contract tests, and a post-rollout incident playbook.
acceptance_criteria: Session-aware SLOs defined: interactive-chat p50 <= 45ms, p95 <= 220ms, p99 <= 700ms for warm-KV sessions (90th percentile of session lengths).

Cold-session allowances: document explicit degraded bands for cold KV warming with p95 <= 500ms and p99 <= 1.5s for first-token only; these are excluded from primary availability SLA but visible in dashboards.

Error budget calculation: per-tenant monthly budget computed from weighted requests where weight = 1 + floor(session_tokens/512) and fallbacks count as 2x failures; automated burn_rate metric exposed.
Canary dose-scaling gates: each dose step passes automated checks for 30m probe windows with criteria: burn_rate <= 0.1 of budget, p99 tail within 10% of baseline, error_rate delta <= 0.05 absolute.
Tenant-fairness guardrail: no single tenant may see >5% of canary traffic during early doses; tenant bucket enforcement validated by synthetic tenant-probes and quota checks.
Monitoring: dashboards for session latency breakdown (cold/warm), per-tenant burn, 1m and 5m rolling probe pass rate, and alerting rules created in PagerDuty with escalation paths.
Automated rollback: CI/CD will auto-trigger rollback if two consecutive dose windows fail gate checks or if cumulative burn exceeds 50% of projected monthly budget in first 48h.
Documentation: Runbook published in Confluence with links to probe harness, dashboard links, and playbook; onboarding doc for on-call to interpret session-aware metrics.
Contract tests: end-to-end integration tests in CI that simulate long-lived sessions (100–200 messages) and validate p95/p99 regressions <5% compared to baseline.
Post-rollout review: 7-day retrospective with metrics and bug list; acceptance only after remediation of any high-severity regressions affecting >1% stable traffic.
rollout_plan: Preparation: create probe harness (synthetic sessions) with 1000 unique sessions across regions; seed probes with both short (1–3 messages) and long (50+ message) conversations.
Baseline collection: run probes for 72 hours on current stable variant to establish warm/cold baselines and per-tenant latency distribution.
Dose 0 -> 1%: apply canary to reserved fleet; 30m probe window; must pass gates to proceed.
1% -> 5%: 60m probe window with additional per-tenant checks; enforce tenant cap and validate billing isolation tags.
5% -> 20%: 2h probe window and SRE validation; manual approval required if any non-critical regressions observed.
20% -> 50%: 3h probe window; increase synthetic probe intensity and run contract tests; require sign-off from SRE and PM.
50% -> 100%: final 24h observation window with escalations in place; full rollout conditional on sustained burn_rate < threshold.
Emergency rollback triggers: doubled error rate, p99 > 2x baseline, or critical customer-impacting errors; immediate CD rollback and SRE paging.

Canary tuning: 'dose-scaling' means we proportionally increase traffic for tenants in a manner that preserves per-tenant fairness using weighted randomization and tenant caps; implement as TrafficShaper config in routing service.
Post-rollout: run 7-day retention probes and generate postmortem regardless of visible incidents to capture performance drift and cost impact.
